newsitem.title: POLAND: Hachette may start own Polish chain - min.
newsitem.headline: Hachette may start own Polish chain - min.

text.p: French firm Hachette will create its own distribution network in Poland if the Polish government fails to sell it the kiosk chain Ruch SA, French Foreign Trade Minister Yves Galland said on Wednesday.

Last month, the ministry abandoned a deal,nearly ready, to sell a 75 percent stake in Ruch, which controls 65 percent of the press distribution market in Poland, to a consortium led by Hachette. It invited new bids for the company.
"Hachette wants to operate in Poland through a Polish company but if this proves impossible...it will launch its own operations," Galland, told a news conference.
He said the treasury ministry had treated the Hachette consortium unfairly because it invited new bids for Ruch after the French-led group had unveiled terms of its offer.
"Other interested parties got to know about the offer before they placed theirs," said Galland, who attended a seminar on Polish-French industrial cooperation.
He confirmed that Hachette would ignore the new invitation for bids for Ruch, published last month, but was ready to uphold its offer from the previous tender.
The offer provided for buying the Ruch stake for $83 million, increasing its capital by $45 million and then investing another $155 million, he said.
Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek, also present, said a court would have to decide whether the initial agreement signed with Hachette in December last year was legally binding. @
The agreement was signed by Kaczmarek, considered one of the most liberal politicians in the ruling left-wing coalition, when he was still a deputy treasury minister.
It was later annulled by Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz, a member of the Peasant Party (PSL), which often criticises sale of Polish companies to foreign capital.
Pietrewicz withdrew from the deal after Hachette failed to meet his request to place a better offer for Ruch, which owns 17,000 kiosks nationwide.
Hachette has suggested it might take legal action against the Polish government if it is not allowed to buy Ruch. @

Pietrewicz asked Hachette to improve its offer early this year after media reported that a Polish group, led by Universal and including private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer Multico SA, wanted to pay more for Ruch.
The group offered to pay $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch and pledged to invest a total of $200 million in the company and placed its bid in the new tender.
But Kaczmarek said he thought the French offer was more attractive because it came from an experienced international company and allowed Ruch's speedy privatisation. @
Galland added that Hachette's bid was attractive also because the French company wanted to make Poland a foothold for expansion into other countries in eastern Europe.
